title: Remove the UI block on endpoints that returned 403 Forbidden
body:
### Problem

The UI aborts every future request to any URL that once returned `403 {"detail":"Forbidden"}`, and keeps that block for the **entire page load** (`main.tsx`: a module-level `Set` that is only ever added to, plus a request interceptor that aborts matching requests). The rationale was "permissions won't change mid-session."

That assumption breaks whenever the auth token is refreshed or rotated mid-session — e.g. an auth manager that re-issues the token out of band, or a control plane that momentarily resolves a subject to an empty permission set during a consistency window. A stale/permission-less token makes a batch of requests (a dashboard's polling fan-out) come back `403 Forbidden`; the UI then blocks all those URLs client-side. Even once the token recovers, the endpoints stay dark until the user does a full browser refresh (which wipes the in-memory `Set`).

Also original intent was also performance. Blocking request that would 403, but that doesn't really hold. If a server can serve successful request (much more expensive) it can serve 403 ones for forbidden users. 

### Fix

Remove the block entirely. It also bought little: a `403` short-circuits at the authorization dependency **before** the route handler runs any work, so a permission-denied request is *cheaper* than a successful one — blocking it saves no meaningful server load. The `401` / invalid-JWT-`403` login-redirect is kept as-is.
